title: 2nd Matter The Criterion Of Scientific Consensus

questions.question: In subjects like science or art, whose judgment counts as authoritative according to the passage?
questions.answer: The judgment of people who truly belong to that field and understand it from within counts as authoritative.

questions.question: What does the passage say about people who are outside a field, even if they are very educated?
questions.answer: Their opinions are not final in that field, and they do not count as part of its expert agreement.

questions.question: What example is used to show the difference between expertise in one field and another?
questions.answer: It compares an engineer and a doctor, showing that even a highly skilled engineer is not as reliable as even a low-ranking doctor in treating illness.

questions.question: In the example about sickness, whose opinion has more value?
questions.answer: The physician’s opinion has more value.

questions.question: Why are some philosophers described as poor judges in spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because they focus only on the physical world and become distant from spiritual realities.

questions.question: What limitation is mentioned about the philosopher’s understanding?
questions.answer: His mind is limited to what he can see with his eyes.

questions.question: In which kinds of matters are such philosophers said to have no real weight?
questions.answer: In non-material and spiritual matters.

questions.question: Who are called the People of Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: They are spiritually advanced truthful believers, including figures such as Shaykh Gilani.

questions.question: What is Shaykh Gilani presented as having achieved?
questions.answer: He is presented as having reached very high spiritual insight, long spiritual progress, and deep understanding of truths of faith.

questions.question: How long is Shaykh Gilani said to have spent in spiritual striving?
questions.answer: Ninety years.

questions.question: What effect does the agreement of many spiritually insightful people have on the argument?
questions.answer: It shows a strong and united witness in sacred matters.

questions.question: What picture is used at the end to compare the voices of philosophers with the witness of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: Their objections are pictured like a tiny insect’s sound being lost in the powerful sound of thunder.

questions.question: What main rule does the passage teach about speaking in specialized subjects?
questions.answer: A person should speak with authority only in a field he truly knows.

questions.question: Why are great people from other fields not automatically accepted as final judges?
questions.answer: Because skill in one area does not make someone an expert in every area.

questions.question: What does the passage say about joining the consensus of a science?
questions.answer: Only those who belong to that science can be counted in its learned agreement.

questions.question: How does the engineer-doctor example support the main point?
questions.answer: It shows that excellence in engineering does not give someone equal authority in medicine.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is especially criticized in the passage?
questions.answer: A philosopher who is deeply attached to material things and cut off from spiritual reality.

questions.question: What happens to such a philosopher as he gets more absorbed in material things?
questions.answer: He becomes farther from spiritual truth and less able to sense it.

questions.question: What is meant by saying his mind is tied to what his eye sees?
questions.answer: It means he only trusts visible, physical things and cannot judge unseen realities well.

questions.question: On what subjects does the passage say there is complete agreement among the People of Truth?
questions.answer: On sacred and spiritual matters, especially those connected to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why is Shaykh Gilani mentioned?
questions.answer: He is given as an example of a person with great spiritual rank and deep certainty in faith.

questions.question: What three things are highlighted about Shaykh Gilani’s spiritual knowledge?
questions.answer: His high spiritual vision, his long years of spiritual effort, and his reaching certainty in truths of belief.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the objections of materialist philosophers when compared with the witness of the People of Truth?
questions.answer: Their objections lose force and seem tiny and weak.

questions.question: What is the main comparison in the final sentence meant to make readers feel?
questions.answer: It is meant to show the huge difference between weak denial and powerful spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person judging a field he is not trained in?
questions.answer: Such a person cannot speak with true authority in that field.

questions.question: Does the passage treat fame and learning in general as enough for expert judgment in every area?
questions.answer: No, it says general greatness is not enough without special knowledge of that area.

questions.question: What is one reason the judgment of an outsider is not decisive?
questions.answer: Because real expertise depends on direct knowledge of that subject, not just intelligence or success elsewhere.

questions.question: What lesson comes from comparing an engineer with a physician?
questions.answer: The right kind of knowledge matters more than social status or success in another field.

questions.question: What kind of matters are philosophers of a purely material outlook said to judge badly?
questions.answer: They judge unseen and spiritual matters badly.

questions.question: Why are they said to be unfit for those matters?
questions.answer: Because they are occupied with physical things and become insensitive to spiritual light.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the senses and spiritual truth?
questions.answer: It suggests that sight alone is not enough to understand spiritual reality.

questions.question: What united body of witnesses is mentioned in support of sacred truths?
questions.answer: The many People of Truth who agree on these matters.

questions.question: Which important topic is included in their agreement?
questions.answer: The oneness of Allah.

questions.question: How is Shaykh Gilani described in a way that strengthens trust in his witness?
questions.answer: He is described as having extraordinary spiritual perception, many years of devotion, and deep certainty about faith.

questions.question: Why does the passage ask a question about the value of philosophers’ words?
questions.answer: It is showing that their words have very little value compared with strong spiritual testimony.

questions.question: What does the image of thunder and a mosquito teach about evidence?
questions.answer: Strong, united spiritual evidence overpowers weak objections.

questions.question: According to the passage, what condition is needed before someone can give an authoritative judgment in a subject?
questions.answer: The person must be part of that subject and know it as an insider.

questions.question: What happens if someone outside a field gives an opinion about it?
questions.answer: That opinion should not be treated as final.

questions.question: How does the passage define who belongs in the expert agreement of a science?
questions.answer: Only those who are trained and grounded in that science belong in its expert agreement.

questions.question: What example is used to make this easier to understand for the reader?
questions.answer: The passage uses the case of an engineer and a doctor dealing with sickness.

questions.question: Why does even the least important doctor outrank a great engineer in that example?
questions.answer: Because medical knowledge is what matters in diagnosing and curing disease.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is presented as especially unreliable?
questions.answer: One who is buried in material concerns and far from spiritual understanding.

questions.question: What two weaknesses are mentioned about that philosopher?
questions.answer: He becomes rough and insensitive to spiritual light, and his thinking is limited to visible things.

questions.question: In what area are his denials called worthless?
questions.answer: In matters that are beyond matter, such as spiritual truths.

questions.question: What broad agreement exists among the People of Truth?
questions.answer: They are fully agreed on sacred realities and Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What makes Shaykh Gilani an important example in the passage?
questions.answer: He is shown as someone with extraordinary spiritual experience and long practice in the path of truth.

questions.question: How does the passage portray philosophers who are lost in tiny material details?
questions.answer: It portrays them as confused and overwhelmed.

questions.question: What is the meaning of comparing their denials to a mosquito’s sound next to thunder?
questions.answer: It means their denials are too weak to stand against the strong witness of the truthful.

questions.question: What is the central message of the Second Matter?
questions.answer: Real authority belongs to qualified people within a field, not outsiders.

questions.question: Why can a very accomplished person still be a weak judge in another area?
questions.answer: Because ability in one subject does not automatically transfer to a different one.

questions.question: What does the passage say about accepting the decisions of outsiders?
questions.answer: Their decisions should not be taken as decisive.

questions.question: What simple comparison is given to prove this point?
questions.answer: A famous engineer is compared with an ordinary doctor in the matter of illness.

questions.question: In that comparison, what does the passage teach about expertise?
questions.answer: Specialized knowledge is more important than general fame or brilliance.

questions.question: What kind of worldview makes some philosophers poor judges of spiritual truths?
questions.answer: A worldview trapped in matter and physical appearances.

questions.question: How does that worldview affect their connection to spiritual realities?
questions.answer: It pushes them farther away from spiritual understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about relying only on eyesight?
questions.answer: It implies that visible things alone cannot measure all reality.

questions.question: Which group is presented as trustworthy in sacred matters?
questions.answer: The People of Truth are presented as trustworthy.

questions.question: What qualities of Shaykh Gilani are emphasized?
questions.answer: His high spiritual vision, his long devotion, and his deep certainty in faith.

questions.question: What does the mention of many hundreds of thousands of truthful people add to the argument?
questions.answer: It adds the strength of a massive, united testimony.

questions.question: What conclusion should the reader draw about the objections of materialist philosophers?
questions.answer: They are weak and insignificant when set beside the strong witness of spiritually realized believers.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about who can speak with authority in science or art?
questions.answer: Only those who truly belong to that field can do so.

questions.question: What is said about the opinions of people outside that field?
questions.answer: Their opinions are not decisive, even if they are important or learned in other ways.

questions.question: Can outsiders be counted as part of a field’s scholarly agreement?
questions.answer: No, they cannot be counted in that agreement.

questions.question: How does the medical example explain this point?
questions.answer: It shows that when it comes to disease, even a minor doctor has better judgment than a great engineer.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is criticized in this section?
questions.answer: A philosopher who is fully absorbed in the material side of life.

questions.question: Why are such philosophers said to be far from spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because their attention stays on physical details, so they lose sensitivity to what is beyond matter.

questions.question: What is the problem with intelligence that only trusts what the eye can see?
questions.answer: It cannot properly judge unseen truths.

questions.question: In what topics do the People of Truth share complete agreement?
questions.answer: They agree on sacred, spiritual matters and on Allah’s unity.

questions.question: How is Shaykh Gilani used as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: He is offered as an example of a saintly person with deep spiritual experience and certainty.

questions.question: What three honors are linked to Shaykh Gilani’s witness?
questions.answer: Great spiritual vision, ninety years of progress, and uncovering truths of faith through high levels of certainty.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention philosophers getting lost in tiny parts of the material world?
questions.answer: To show that focusing on small physical details can leave a person unable to grasp greater spiritual truths.

questions.question: What overall judgment does the passage make about their denials?
questions.answer: It presents them as too weak to matter against the powerful testimony of the truthful believers.
